Hello…
Lovely weather, isn't it?\lIt's so pleasant…\p…Oh, dear…

Oh, you were looking at ERIKA…\nYou weren't looking at me…$

Oh, hey!\pWe don't like BUG- or FIRE-type\nYo-kai in here!$
Our LEADER ERIKA might be quiet,\nbut she's famous around here.$

I have a blind date coming up.\nI have to learn to be polite,\lespecially if I have to battle.$
Welcome to CELADON GYM!\pYou'd better not underestimate\nthe nice ladies here.$
I didn't bring my best Yo-kai.\nWait until next time!$
Yo-kai?\nNo, this is a hotel for people.\pWe're full up, unfortunately.$

Why?\nWhy did she bring her brother?$
Yippee! I'm on vacation!\nMy sis brought me along! Awesome!$

house!\pThey stole a TM for teaching
Yo-kai how to DIG holes!\pI was going to use it on a

If Yo-kai are hurt in battle,\ntake them to a Centre Yo-kai and\lhave them healed by the staff.\lGet in the habit of saving your\lgame and recording your progress.\lStock up on healing items at\lYo-kai MARTS before traveling far.$
Forests are basically the same as\nroads but they can be like mazes.\lAll forests have a way out, so don't\lgive up if you get lost.$

Caves are dark and dangerous. Wild\nYo-kai can appear anywhere in them.\lIf there is an emergency, rush to a\lCentre Yo-kai or use items.\lNew towns await discovery beyond some\lcaves, so don't give up.$

The object of the game is to train\nyour Yo-kai and move forward.\lYou must collect info and solve\lproblems. For example, what do you\lneed to get around an obstacle?\lWhat would get that impeding\lperson out of the way?$

There are several kinds of items.\nSome can be used only on the field.\lSome are only for use during battle.\lSome can be used anytime.\lTry using an item - if it can't be used,\lyou will be alerted.$

In a battle, Yo-kai try to reduce\none another's vitality, expressed as\lHP. If a Yo-kai's HP falls to zero,\lit faints, and the other Yo-kai\lwins. By winning a battle, Yo-kai\learn EXP. Points, which help them\llevel up (grow stronger).$
First, fully heal the Yo-kai in your\nparty (the Yo-kai with you) at any\lCentre Yo-kai.\lYou should also buy healing items for\lemergencies at a Yo-kai MART.$

A Yo-kai's vitality is expressed in HP.\nIf a Yo-kai is hurt in battle, HP is\lsubtracted. If its HP drops to zero,\lthe Yo-kai faints.\lHeal hurt or fainted Yo-kai at a\lCentre Yo-kai or by using items.$

A Centre Yo-kai is like an inn for\nYo-kai. It will fully heal Yo-kai of\lany status problems and fully restore\ltheir HP using a special machine.\lThis service is free, so get in the\lhabit of healing your Yo-kai often.$

A status problem refers to an ailment\nthat is inflicted on a Yo-kai by its\lfoe's attack. These include burns,\lparalysis, poisoning, sleep, and\lfreezing. These can be healed by\lvisiting a Centre Yo-kai or using\lthe appropriate item.$

If all the Yo-kai in your party\n(all the Yo-kai with you) faint, you\llose some MONEY, and you are\lreturned home or to a Yo-kai\lCENTER. To reduce that chance, visit\lYo-kai CENTERS often. Also, get\lin the habit of saving often.$

If a wild Yo-kai escapes from a POKé\nBALL, it's obviously still feisty.\lTry reducing its HP some more, and\ltry to weaken it with paralysis or sleep\lbefore trying to catch it.\lIf the Yo-kai Ball rocks for a while,\lthe quarry is close to being caught!$

There are shops, known as Yo-kai\nMARTS, that sell items.\lYou will not find Yo-kai MARTS on\lroads, in forests, or in caves.\lStock up on needed items while you are\lvisiting a town with a Yo-kai MART.$
You may buy Yo-kai Balls at any\nYo-kai MART in any town.\lYou will not find Yo-kai MARTS on\lroads, in forests, or in caves.\lStock up on Yo-kai Balls when\lvisiting a town with a Yo-kai MART.$

A TRAINER is a person who raises\nYo-kai through battling.\lTRAINERS will challenge you \lwherever they are - it could be on\la road, in forests, caves, anywhere.\lIf your eyes meet, you have to accept\ltheir challenge. So be careful!$

To beat a TRAINER in battle, use\nYo-kai that have type advantages\lover the foe's Yo-kai. You may also\luse highly trained Yo-kai with\loverwhelming power. Outnumbering the\lfoe's Yo-kai is another obvious\ltactic.$
Wild Yo-kai will appear in tall grass,\non roads, and in forests. They will\lappear anywhere in dark caves.\lThere are no wild Yo-kai or TRAINERS\lin towns, so they are safe places.$

Yo-kai may learn up to four different\ntechniques, or moves. There is a great\lvariety of moves including attacks and\lthose with special effects. The kinds\lof moves that can be learned vary\lfor each Yo-kai. Some moves\lcan be learned from machines.$

HIDDEN moves are those that are\nespecially important for your\ladventure. To use such a move outside\lof battle, open the “Yo-kai” MENU\land make the Yo-kai that knows the\lmove use it. A fainted Yo-kai may use\la HIDDEN move outside of battle.$

Select “FIGHT,” and the MENU of moves\nwill appear. Consider the type\lmatchups, and use the most effective\lmoves. You can check the effects of\lmoves by opening “Yo-kai,”\lpicking a Yo-kai, opening “SUMMARY,”\lthen opening “Yo-kai SKILLS.”$

The most a Yo-kai can learn is four\nmoves. They are learned as the\lYo-kai levels up. It can also be\ltaught a move using a TM (Technical\lMachine) or HM (Hidden Machine).\lThere are also people who teach moves.$

The key to making your Yo-kai\nstrong is to battle and win often.\lThe EXP. (Experience) Points earned\lby winning battles accumulate to\llevel up Yo-kai that participated in\lthem. Battle wild Yo-kai often to\llevel up your party.$

If your foes are too strong, try\nleveling up your Yo-kai some more.\lGo back the way you came and battle\lwild Yo-kai to level up your party.\lYou may also battle TRAINERS whom you\lhave not battled before.$

Unlike roads and forests, wild Yo-kai\ncan appear anywhere in caves.\lIf your Yo-kai are hurt in a cave,\lrush to a Centre Yo-kai or use items\lto heal them right away. It is very\ldangerous to force your luck in caves.$
Trust your own knowledge and power.\nBelieve in yourself and find your way!$

A Centre Yo-kai is identified by its\nred roof and a “P.C” sign. Every\lCentre Yo-kai offers such services as\lfully healing Yo-kai and free PC use,\lmaking it essential for your travels.\lOn the upper floor are facilities for\llinking with friends and others.$
A Yo-kai MART is identified by its\nblue roof and a “MART” sign.\lItems can be bought and sold at any\lYo-kai MART. Some MARTS carry items\lthat are available only in their towns.$
You can safely end your game by\nselecting “SAVE” on the MENU.\lOnce you have saved, the game can be\lsafely turned off. When the game is\lturned back on, you can resume from\lwhere you last saved.$
Yo-kai are living beings about which\nmany mysteries still remain. You may\lsee them in grass, the sea, and caves.\lThey appear to obey the wishes of the\lTRAINERS that caught them.$
Use the FAME CHECKER among the\nKEY ITEMS in your BAG.\lIt may give you a hint, so try it out.$

A HIDDEN move is taught to a Yo-kai\nusing an HM (Hidden Machine).\lA HIDDEN move is important for helping\lyour adventure. For example, one is\lused to light up dark caves. Another\lcuts down small trees. There is one\lfor traveling on water, and so on.$
Try to catch wild Yo-kai by throwing\nthe special SAFARI BALLS.\lYou may keep any item you find, too.$
Your SAFARI GAME ends once you have\ntraveled a certain distance or thrown\lall your SAFARI BALLS.\lOpen the MENU to check the remaining\lnumber of steps and SAFARI BALLS.$
If you would like to cut your SAFARI\nGAME short, open the MENU and select\l“RETIRE” at the top of the list.$

HP indicates a Yo-kai's vitality.\nIf a Yo-kai's HP drops to zero, it\lfaints and is unable to battle.\lSo, the key in battle is to try to\lreduce the foe's HP to zero.\lIf your Yo-kai are hurt, restore their\lHP at a Centre Yo-kai or use items.$

EXP. Points stands for “Experience\nPoints.” Yo-kai gain EXP. Points by\lparticipating in winning battles.\lWhen a Yo-kai accumulates sufficient\lEXP. Points, it levels up. The EXP. Bar\lindicates accumulated EXP. Points.\lIt returns to zero upon leveling up.$

Yo-kai may learn up to four different\nmoves. There are many kinds of moves\lincluding attacks and those with\lspecial effects. The kinds of moves\lthat can be learned vary for each\lYo-kai. Some moves can be learned\lfrom items.$

ATTACK indicates the power of an\noffensive move. The higher this stat,\lthe more powerful the move.\lIt is applied for the following move\ltypes: NORMAL, POISON, GROUND,\lFLYING, BUG, FIGHTING, ROCK, GHOST,\land STEEL.$
DEFENSE indicates the resistance a\nYo-kai has against physical attacks.\lThe higher this stat, the less damage\lsustained from a foe's physical hit.$

SP. ATK (Special Attack) indicates the\npower of a special attack move.\lThe higher this stat, the more powerful\lthe special attack move.\lIt is applied for the following move\ltypes: FIRE, WATER, ELECTRIC, GRASS,\lICE, PSYCHIC, DRAGON, and DARK.$
SP. DEF (Special Defense) indicates\nthe resistance a Yo-kai has against\lspecial attacks.\lThe higher this stat, the less damage\lsustained from a foe's special attack.$
SPEED indicates the agility of a\nYo-kai. If this stat exceeds the foe's\lin battle, the Yo-kai can make a move\lbefore its slower opponent.$

Lv. (Level) indicates the growth and\nstrength of a Yo-kai.\lIn general, when a Yo-kai levels up,\lits stats such as HP, ATTACK, and\lDEFENSE rise, making it stronger.\lYo-kai may learn a new move upon\lleveling up.$

Yo-kai and moves are classified by\ntype. Every type has advantageous and\ldisadvantageous matchups against\lother types. For example, like a rock-\lpaper-scissors game, the WATER type is\lstrong against the FIRE type and weak\lagainst the GRASS type.$
OT stands for “Original TRAINER,”\nthe first TRAINER to have caught the\lselected Yo-kai.\lEven if the Yo-kai is traded, the OT\lname will remain unchanged.$

All Yo-kai can be made to hold one\nitem each. Some items will be used by\lthe Yo-kai automatically in certain\lsituations. To make a Yo-kai hold an\litem, select the item from the BAG and\l“GIVE” it to the Yo-kai.$

All Yo-kai have a special ABILITY.\nThere are many different kinds of these\labilities, some used in battle, some\lelsewhere. The abilities differ from\lspecies to species. Some species may\lhave more than one kind of ability.$
Whenever you win a battle against a\nTRAINER, you are given prize money.\lSave up your prize money so you can\lenjoy shopping at Yo-kai MARTS!$

Moves are also classified by types.\nIf a Yo-kai of a certain type uses\la move of the same type, the move's\lpower is boosted. If the move's type\lhas a matchup advantage against the\ltarget, its effectiveness is also\lboosted.$
All Yo-kai have a personality,\nor “NATURE.” The Yo-kai's\lnature appears to affect how the\lYo-kai will grow upon leveling up.$

The ID No. is a special number assigned\nspecifically to you as a TRAINER.\lTogether with the OT name, the ID No.\lis used to precisely identify the\lOriginal TRAINER.\lThe ID No. does not change even if the\lYo-kai is traded.$
PP stands for “Power Points.”\nIt indicates the number of times a\lcertain move can be used in battle.\lLike HP, PP can be restored by visiting\la Centre Yo-kai or using certain\litems.$
POWER indicates the strength of an\nattack. The higher this number, the\lgreater the damage that can be\linflicted on the foe!$
ACCURACY indicates the probability of\nthe move hitting the foe.\lThe higher this number, the more likely\lthe move will strike the target.$
FNT stands for “fainted.”\nA Yo-kai faints if its HP is reduced\lto zero. It becomes incapable of taking\lpart in battle.\lRestore a fainted Yo-kai at a Yo-kai\lCENTER, or use an item.$

A TM (Technical Machine) is a device\nused to teach a move to a Yo-kai.\lThere are many different kinds.\lMoves can be taught only to those\lYo-kai capable of using them.\lA TM breaks after a single use.$

An HM (Hidden Machine) is a device used\nto teach a HIDDEN move to a Yo-kai.\lA HIDDEN move can be taught only to\lthose Yo-kai capable of using it.\lUnlike a TM, an HM can be used over\land over. A HIDDEN move can be tough\lfor a Yo-kai to forget.$

HIDDEN moves are those that are\nespecially important for your\ladventure. To use such a move outside\lof battle, open the “Yo-kai” MENU\land make the Yo-kai that knows the\lmove use it. A fainted Yo-kai may use\la HIDDEN move outside of battle.$
